meta.label: Chord view
meta.function: The key (top left) and the performance mode (top right) in the bar; the chord's name big, its numeral, the voicing; the voiced notes on a two-octave keyboard (lit white keys: a block at the foot; lit black keys: hollow).
meta.description: The name stays until the next chord, as on the FM-1's Chord view.

items.text:
Pads, rows 1-3: degrees I..VII and I' of the key, bottom row C3; each plays the scale's chord (Key Mode). The tonic yellow, the sounding chord's tones cyan, the pressed pad white.
Top row: DIM MIN MAJ SUS (violet), 6 m7 M7 9 (orange); held or locked, they override the scale's chord. Two types: the last pressed (MIN + MAJ = SUS).
Steps: the 16 progressions (lit: the six that have chords).

items.name: 2. CHORDS: Chromatic (Menu)
items.description: For chords outside the key: rows a 4th apart from C3, as Move's chromatic layout. Hold SUS, press Eb: Ebsus.

items.text: Its MIDI (Perform on channel 1, the bass on 2) goes where the Routing page sends ChoralRoot's MIDI: other firmwares, Out.

TAKEOVER (tk1), the rules every firmware shares:
- Track 1 tapped in FM-1 mode: the firmware's takeover (its name shown and said); tapped in the takeover: FM-1 mode. From MIDI / Control / Seq: back to whichever of the two the slot was left in.
- Volume touched + Back: FM-1 mode from any takeover (the only way out when a firmware claims everything).
- What a firmware does not claim keeps RemoteFM1's meaning. ChoralRoot claims all but the Track buttons and Volume.
- Screen reader: "Chords, takeover" on entering, "FM-1 mode" on leaving; the firmware's own words between ("Chord D minor seven").

OPEN QUESTIONS
1. Steps: the 16 progressions (proposed), or something else (performance modes, looper slots)?
2. Chords and bass to different firmwares (a per-channel route in the core), or one route for both?
3. Capture, Sample, Undo: unused here. Ideas?
